a.clean: Probably caught the biggest fish of my life this morning. You should have been there. We went out to the lake at 4:30 because Omar insisted that's when they bite, and for three hours nothing. I was freezing and bored and about to quit, and then my line goes tight and I nearly dropped a rod. It takes me 20 minutes to reel it in, and it's a pike, easily three feet long, I'm not exaggerating. Omar has the photo outside there. We let it go obviously, but my arms are still shaking. The best part is the guy on the next boat was watching the whole time and he gave me a thumbs up, so now I'm famous at the marina. We're going again next Saturday if you want to come.

a.clean: Dear Sophia, I've been putting off this email because I didn't quite know how to say it. I lost my job in March. They laid off about 40 people, and I was one of them, which was a shock, because I'd just been promoted. The first month I was kind of a mess. I slept till noon and watched terrible television. Then I made myself a schedule, get up, go for a walk, apply to three jobs a day, and slowly it started to feel less awful. I had four interviews in May and I started a new company on the 1st of July, so the story has a happy ending. I just didn't want you to hear it from someone else. Thank you for the card you sent. It was exactly what I needed. I'd love to catch up properly. Are you free for a call this Sunday? Let me know. Much love, Breedy

a.clean: The power went out at about 4 yesterday and I was alone with the kids, which was a nightmare. I was prepared though. We have candles, and a camping stove, and a whole box of board games, so we made a fort in the living room, and we ate soup on the stove, and played Monopoly by flashlight. At some point my daughter said, this is the best day ever, and I thought, wow, all it took was a blackout. The power came back at 9 and everyone groaned, which I did not expect. We turned it off again for another hour, just because. My husband got home at 10 and said, what's going on, because the whole house was dark and we were all in a fort. I said, you missed it, and he did.
